ARABIC — MOCK EXAM #16
====

GRADE: Grade 7
SUBJECT: ARABIC
TIME ALLOWED: 2 hours
TOTAL MARKS: 80
EXAM BODY: KJSEA

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show formula → substitution → steps → final answer with units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the best option.
4. Check your work before submitting.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. When practising Listening for Gist, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Copy random text without understanding Listening for Gist.
   B. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Listening for Gist.
   C. Use insults to “practise” Listening for Gist.
   D. Avoid reading anything related to Listening for Gist.

2. In ARABIC, the best classroom habit is: (1 mark)
   A. Only memorise without using the language
   B. Mix random languages with no purpose
   C. Practise listening, speaking, reading, and writing every day
   D. Avoid speaking to classmates

3. When practising Imitative Speaking, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use insults to “practise” Imitative Speaking.
   B. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Imitative Speaking.
   C. Avoid reading anything related to Imitative Speaking.
   D. Copy random text without understanding Imitative Speaking.

4. When practising Phonological Awareness, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Copy random text without understanding Phonological Awareness.
   B. Avoid reading anything related to Phonological Awareness.
   C. Use insults to “practise” Phonological Awareness.
   D. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Phonological Awareness.

5. When practising Listening for Information, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Copy random text without understanding Listening for Information.
   B. Use insults to “practise” Listening for Information.
   C. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Listening for Information.
   D. Avoid reading anything related to Listening for Information.

6. When practising Reading Aloud: Fluency, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Avoid reading anything related to Reading Aloud: Fluency.
   B. Use insults to “practise” Reading Aloud: Fluency.
   C. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Reading Aloud: Fluency.
   D. Copy random text without understanding Reading Aloud: Fluency.

7. When practising Phonological Awareness: Pronunciation, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use insults to “practise” Phonological Awareness: Pronunciation.
   B. Avoid reading anything related to Phonological Awareness: Pronunciation.
   C. Copy random text without understanding Phonological Awareness: Pronunciation.
   D. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Phonological Awareness: Pronunciation.

8. When practising Imitative Speaking: Pronunciation, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Imitative Speaking: Pronunciation.
   B. Avoid reading anything related to Imitative Speaking: Pronunciation.
   C. Copy random text without understanding Imitative Speaking: Pronunciation.
   D. Use insults to “practise” Imitative Speaking: Pronunciation.

9. When practising Conversational Skills, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Conversational Skills.
   B. Copy random text without understanding Conversational Skills.
   C. Avoid reading anything related to Conversational Skills.
   D. Use insults to “practise” Conversational Skills.

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
10. In three clear sentences, explain Guided Writing: Paragraph Writing and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)
